coalition_name: South Dakota Network Against Family Violence and Sexual Assault
criminal_definition: Stalking is willfully, maliciously, and repeatedly following or harassing another person, making a credible threat intended to place the person in reasonable fear of death or great bodily injury, or repeatedly harassing another person by verbal, electronic, digital media, mechanical, telegraphic, or written communication.
criminal_penalty: Class 1 misdemeanor for a first offense; a second or subsequent conviction within 10 years, or stalking while a protection order is in effect, is a Class 6 felony.
cyber_note: The stalking statute itself covers repeated harassment by means of verbal, electronic, digital media, mechanical, telegraphic, or written communication, so online harassment can be charged as stalking.
order_free_note: There are no costs or fees associated with obtaining or serving a Stalking Protection Order.
order_where: File a petition with the clerk of the circuit court; magistrate courts share jurisdiction over stalking protection orders.

coalition_name: Tennessee Coalition to End Domestic and Sexual Violence
criminal_definition: Stalking is a willful course of conduct involving repeated or continuing harassment of another person that would cause a reasonable person to feel terrorized, frightened, intimidated, threatened, harassed, or molested, and that actually causes the victim to feel that way.
criminal_penalty: Stalking is a Class A misdemeanor (up to 11 months, 29 days in jail, fine up to $2,500); aggravated stalking is a Class E felony (1 to 6 years, fine up to $3,000); especially aggravated stalking is a Class C felony (3 to 15 years, fine up to $10,000).
cyber_note: Tennessee has no separate cyberstalking statute; the stalking definition expressly includes unconsented contact by electronic communication such as email, text messages, and social media messages.
order_free_note: No filing fee is charged for an order of protection for domestic abuse, stalking, or sexual assault.
order_where: File a sworn petition in circuit, chancery, or general sessions court in the county where you live, where the respondent lives, or where the abuse occurred.

criminal_definition: Stalking is knowingly engaging, on more than one occasion and as part of the same scheme or course of conduct directed at a specific person, in conduct that constitutes harassment or involves threats of bodily injury, death, or property damage, which the actor knows or reasonably should know the other person will regard as threatening.
criminal_penalty: Third-degree felony (2 to 10 years in prison, fine up to $10,000); a second or subsequent stalking conviction is a second-degree felony (2 to 20 years, fine up to $10,000).
cyber_note: Texas has no separate cyberstalking statute; online conduct is prosecuted under the stalking statute, Tex. Penal Code § 42.072, which covers electronic conduct.
order_duration: For the duration of the lives of the offender and victim, or for a shorter period stated in the order; if no period is stated, the order lasts until the second anniversary of the date it was issued.
order_name: Protective Order for Victims of Stalking (Chapter 7B)
order_where: File an application for a protective order under Chapter 7B in the court in the county where you live; no relationship to the offender is required.

criminal_definition: Stalking is intentionally or knowingly engaging in a course of conduct directed at a specific person that the actor knows or should know would cause a reasonable person to fear for their own safety or the safety of another, or to suffer other emotional distress.
criminal_penalty: Class A misdemeanor for a first offense; third-degree felony if the actor has a prior stalking conviction or violated a permanent criminal stalking injunction; second-degree felony if a dangerous weapon was used or the actor has two or more prior stalking convictions.
cyber_note: The stalking statute expressly includes using a computer, the Internet, text messaging, or any other electronic means as part of the course of conduct.
order_duration: Three years from the date the ex parte civil stalking injunction is served
order_where: File a verified written petition in the district court in the judicial district where you or the respondent resides or is temporarily domiciled, or where any of the events occurred.

coalition_name: Vermont Network Against Domestic and Sexual Violence
criminal_definition: Stalking is purposefully engaging in a course of conduct directed at a specific person that the person knows or should know would cause a reasonable person to fear for their safety or the safety of a family member, or to suffer substantial emotional distress.
criminal_penalty: Up to 2 years in prison, a fine up to $5,000, or both; aggravated stalking under 13 V.S.A. § 1063 carries up to 5 years in prison, a fine up to $25,000, or both.
cyber_note: No separate cyberstalking statute was verified from an official source; the stalking definition in 12 V.S.A. § 5131 covers use of an electronic, digital, or geolocation device to surveil a specific person.
order_duration: For a fixed period set by the court, extendable on the plaintiff's motion for such additional time as the court deems necessary to protect the plaintiff
order_free_note: No filing fee is required for an order against stalking or sexual assault.
order_where: File a complaint with the Civil Division of the Superior Court; available only against someone who is not a family or household member.

coalition_name: Virginia Sexual and Domestic Violence Action Alliance
criminal_definition: Stalking is engaging in conduct on more than one occasion with the intent to place another person in reasonable fear of death, criminal sexual assault, or bodily injury to that person or to a family or household member.
criminal_penalty: Class 1 misdemeanor (up to 12 months in jail, fine up to $2,500); a second or subsequent conviction within 5 years is a Class 6 felony (up to 5 years in prison, fine up to $2,500).
cyber_note: No separate cyberstalking statute was verified from an official source.
order_duration: Up to two years, extendable for additional periods of up to two years each on the petitioner's motion
order_free_note: There is no charge to file or serve a protective order petition in Virginia.
order_where: File a petition in General District Court; non-family abuse protective orders cover stalking, threats, or acts of violence by someone who is not a family or household member.

coalition_name: Washington State Coalition Against Domestic Violence & Sexual Assault
criminal_definition: Stalking is intentionally and repeatedly harassing or following another person, or knowingly installing or monitoring an electronic tracking device without consent to track another person's location, in a way that would cause a reasonable person to feel frightened, intimidated, or harassed.
criminal_penalty: Gross misdemeanor (up to 364 days in jail, fine up to $5,000); Class B felony (up to 10 years in prison, fine up to $20,000) if aggravating factors apply, such as a prior harassment or stalking conviction, violation of a protective order, or use of a deadly weapon.
cyber_note: Cyber harassment is making an electronic communication with intent to harass, intimidate, or torment another person; it is a gross misdemeanor, or a Class C felony if aggravating factors apply.
order_duration: One year from the date of the order, unless a different end date is listed in the order
order_free_note: An antiharassment protection order carries a filing fee (about $53), waived if the conduct includes stalking, a hate crime, violence, or a threat of violence, or if the petitioner cannot pay.
order_where: File a petition in district court or superior court in the county where you live.

coalition_name: West Virginia Coalition Against Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: Stalking is engaging in a course of conduct directed at another person with the intent to cause that person to fear for their personal safety, the safety of others, or to suffer substantial emotional distress.
criminal_penalty: Misdemeanor: fine up to $1,000, up to 6 months in jail, or both; a second or subsequent conviction is a felony (1 to 5 years in a state correctional facility, fine $3,000 to $10,000).
cyber_note: No separate cyberstalking statute was verified from an official source.
order_free_note: No filing fee is charged for a personal safety order petition under W. Va. Code § 53-8-13.
order_where: File a petition with the magistrate court in the county where you live, where the respondent lives, or where the abuse occurred.

criminal_definition: Stalking is intentionally engaging in a course of conduct directed at a specific person that would cause a reasonable person under the same circumstances to suffer serious emotional distress or to fear bodily injury to or the death of themselves or a member of their family or household.
criminal_penalty: Class I felony (up to 3.5 years in prison, fine up to $10,000); Class H felony (up to 6 years) with prior convictions; Class F felony (up to 12.5 years, fine up to $25,000) in the most serious cases.
cyber_note: No separate cyberstalking statute was verified from an official source; the course of conduct in Wis. Stat. § 940.32 includes electronic contact such as text messages and social media.
order_free_note: A filing fee applies, but it can be waived under Wis. Stat. § 814.61(1)(e) for petitioners who cannot pay.
order_where: File a petition with the clerk of the circuit court in the county where you live; no domestic relationship with the respondent is required.

coalition_name: Wyoming Coalition Against Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault
criminal_definition: Stalking is engaging, with intent to harass another person, in a course of conduct reasonably likely to harass that person, including communicating with, following, or placing the person under surveillance by electronic, digital, or GPS means.
criminal_penalty: Misdemeanor: up to 1 year in jail, fine up to $750, or both; felony stalking (prior conviction, serious bodily harm, violation of a protection order, or other statutory triggers): up to 10 years in prison.
cyber_note: The stalking statute expressly covers using any electronic, digital, or global positioning system device to communicate with, follow, or surveil the victim.
order_duration: Up to three years, extendable for additional periods of up to one year each
order_free_note: There is no fee to file the petition or to have it served.
order_where: File a petition in the circuit court in the county where you live, where the stalker lives or is found, or where the stalking occurred; no special relationship with the stalker is required.
